source.check: returned unopposed: Andrews's own election notice thanks 'the Electors of the Comber Electoral Division for the honour they have paid me in again returning me unopposed their representative [on] County Down County Council', signed 'JOHN M. ANDREWS, 7th May. 1936.' (Northern Whig, 8 May 1936, p. 6)

note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 13 April 1936, p. 10). There were no contests. The 1936 reports name only the three changes (Bangor, Garvaghy, Portaferry: Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15; Dromore Leader, 9 May 1936, p. 2) and Comber (J. M. Andrews's election notice, Northern Whig, 8 May 1936); no one was nominated for Dromore (Irish News, 8 May 1936, p. 5: 'a co-option will be necessary'). Six more divisions (Gilford, Holywood, Newry, Newtownards, Rathfriland, Saintfield) are recorded from the report of the new council's first meeting on 18 June 1936; the other nine are not recorded (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Sitting member; the notice is dated 7 May 1936, before the 4 June poll. Returned unopposed.
